sowhat.text: With the 10-year at 5.07% and Waller pointing to a 50 bp hike in December, financing stays expensive, but high yield spreads near 343 bp show credit is open. Strategic buyers are still paying up for AI and security assets, and energy and power sales keep closing.

pitch: Stocks were mixed on Wednesday. The S&P 500 slipped 0.2 percent to about 7,324, the Dow fell 1.1 percent, and the Nasdaq rose 0.4 percent. The Fed minutes were hawkish, nearly every official saw more hikes as likely, and Governor Waller said a half-point move is probably needed in December. The 10-year ended at 5.07 percent. Oil fell, with WTI at about 83 dollars and Brent near 92, on rising US stockpiles. On deals, Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute for 4.5 billion dollars in stock, ECP closed EnergySolutions, and NRG is selling six gas plants to LS Power for 4 billion. Anthropic priced its IPO above range and starts trading today.

quiz.q: Where did WTI crude settle on Wednesday 18 Nov?
quiz.a: $83.26, down $2.75 (3.2%), on a rise in US crude and fuel stockpiles.

quiz.q: Why did the Fed minutes and Waller matter for rates on 18 Nov?
quiz.a: Nearly all officials saw further hikes as likely appropriate, and Waller said a half-point hike is probably needed on Dec 8-9, which keeps the 10-year near 5.07%.

quiz.q: How is Palo Alto Networks paying for Applied Compute, and for how much?
quiz.a: All stock, valued at $4.5B, expected to close in its fiscal Q3 2027.

chat.a: Stocks were mixed on Wednesday: the S&P 500 fell 0.2% to 7,324, the Dow fell 1.1% and the Nasdaq rose 0.4%. The Fed minutes were hawkish and Waller said a half-point hike is probably needed in December. The 10-year is 5.07%, so rates are the backdrop.
chat.tip: Lead with the Fed, then Nvidia.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: WTI settled at $83.26, down 3.2%, and Brent at $91.95, down 1.3%, a spread of about $9. The move was tied to rising US crude and fuel stockpiles. Lower oil pressures upstream valuations, which matters when buyers and sellers are pricing energy deals.
chat.tip: Say what would change your view.

chat.a: Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute for $4.5B in stock on 18 Nov. ECP closed its EnergySolutions buyout on 16 Nov, with Morgan Stanley and RBC advising EnergySolutions. NRG is selling six gas plants to LS Power for $4B, about 8.0x 2027 EBITDA, advised by Barclays.
chat.tip: Name the advisers; bankers will ask.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut on Thursday, since a strong first day would confirm the IPO window for large AI issuers. After that, the December 8-9 FOMC, where Waller has argued for a half-point hike.
chat.tip: Tie each event to financing conditions.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 5.07% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Long-duration assets with most of their value in the terminal value are hit hardest.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: How do high rates affect a sponsor deal like ECP and EnergySolutions?
chat.a: A 10-year at 5.07% and a Fed possibly hiking 50 bp raise the cost of acquisition debt, which squeezes sponsor returns unless the price adjusts. High yield spreads were 343 bp on 17 Nov, so credit is available, just at a high all-in cost.
chat.tip: Separate the base rate from the credit spread.

chat.q: Why would an acquirer pay in stock, as Palo Alto Networks is doing for Applied Compute?
chat.a: An all-stock deal avoids borrowing at today's high rates, with the 10-year at 5.07%, and shares risk with the target's owners. The catch is that it dilutes existing holders and depends on the acquirer's share price, which makes a volatile tape matter more.
